report.title: Auto Mode Loses Its Fallback, Kimi K3.1 Lands in vLLM, and the Compute Bill Comes Due
report.lede: Two threads dominate today's catalog: coding agents tightening their own safety and identity surfaces (Claude Code's auto-mode server check, Codex's runtime auth and privacy mod), and inference stacks racing to absorb a new model family (Kimi K3.1 across vLLM's model, decode, and Rust frontend layers). Underneath both, the RL and serving literature keeps grinding on the same question — where does the compute actually go?
executiveSummary: Claude Code v2.1.319 removes the silent fallback to the built-in classifier when auto mode's server-side check is unavailable, converting an availability failure into an explicit ask-or-deny decision.

vLLM's Kimi K3.1 work arrives as a split covering model files, NVIDIA-specific decode, and a Rust frontend chat renderer — a signal that the Rust frontend is now a first-class target for new model support.
RL papers this cycle converge on cost accounting: OPD vs GRPO FLOPs, LoRA spectral dynamics under RL versus SFT, and safe-RL under massively parallel short-horizon rollouts.
highlights: Claude Code auto mode no longer degrades to a local classifier when telemetry or feature flags are off — unchecked calls are asked about or denied.
vLLM lands Kimi K3.1 model files plus NVIDIA specialized decode, with the chat renderer going through the Rust frontend.
vLLM sleep mode level 2 now discards only parameters, a narrower memory-reclamation contract than before.
A preprint compares on-policy distillation against GRPO on held-out accuracy per training FLOP — unverified, but the right axis.
MCP schema fixes restore optional _meta on input requests and responses after SEP-2322 dropped it as a side effect.

stories.title: Claude Code Auto Mode Stops Falling Back to the Local Classifier
whatHappened: anthropics/claude-code v2.1.319 changes auto mode so that when telemetry or feature flags are off — including behind LLM gateways — calls the server cannot check are asked about or denied, with no fallback to the built-in classifier; setting CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=0 keeps the old behavior, and Bedrock, Vertex, and Foundry are unchanged.
The release also changes gateway behavior: CLAUDE_CODE_AUTO_MODE_SERVER=1 turns on the server-side check even with CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_EXPERIMENTAL_BETAS set.
mechanism: Auto mode previously had two decision paths: a server-side check and a local classifier. When the server path was unreachable, the client silently substituted the local classifier, meaning the effective policy depended on network and flag state rather than on a single configured authority. v2.1.319 collapses that into one authority — if the server cannot adjudicate, the action is escalated to the user or refused.
whyItMatters: For teams running Claude Code behind a gateway or with telemetry disabled, the permission model changes shape: fewer silent approvals, more prompts. That is the correct trade for a tool with shell access, but it will surface as friction in air-gapped or privacy-restricted deployments.
applicability: Relevant to platform teams operating Claude Code behind LLM gateways or with experimental betas disabled. Do not generalize the Bedrock/Vertex/Foundry exemption to other providers — the release names only those three.

stories.title: Claude Code Ships a Privacy Mod That Blocks Shell Calls Leaking Account Identity
whatHappened: anthropics/claude-code: mods: add the privacy mod (#107768). anthropics/claude-code commit "mods: add the privacy mod (#107768)" adds the source of a built-in that refuses a shell call holding the signed-in account's email address and naming a User-Agent, and declares $.session.identity in mods/types for the mod to read.
A follow-up commit in the same PR documents what else turns the mod off.
mechanism: The mod is a policy layer over tool invocation rather than a prompt instruction: it inspects the outgoing shell command for the session's identity fields and rejects the call before execution. Declaring $.session.identity in the mod type schema means the identity is a typed input to the policy, not scraped from environment state.
whyItMatters: This is the pattern worth copying — enforcement at the tool boundary, with the sensitive datum as an explicit typed dependency. Prompt-level 'don't leak my email' instructions are advisory; a pre-execution check is not.
applicability: Coding-agent platform teams and anyone building mod/plugin systems with access to session identity. The commit describes one specific leak vector (email plus User-Agent in a shell call); it is not a general exfiltration defense.

stories.title: Codex Routes Realtime Connections Through Runtime Authentication
whatHappened: openai/codex: Apply runtime authentication to realtime connections (#60003). openai/codex commit "Apply runtime authentication to realtime connections (#60003)" states that realtime connections bypassed runtime authentication and reused captured authentication headers for sideband handshakes.

The change applies runtime authentication to realtime WebSocket connections, WebRTC call creation, and sideband attachment when enabled for supported OpenAI destinations, resolving credentials across call creation, retries, and reconnects.
mechanism: Captured headers are a snapshot: once a token is baked into a handshake, retries and reconnects replay a stale credential and ignore the user's selected credential source. Threading runtime authentication through the connection lifecycle makes credential resolution a per-attempt operation rather than a per-session one.
whyItMatters: Long-lived realtime sessions are exactly where token rotation and credential-source switching break. Fixing this at the transport layer removes a class of auth bugs that only appear after the first reconnect.
applicability: Teams embedding Codex realtime features or building similar WebSocket/WebRTC agent transports. The commit scopes the behavior to supported OpenAI destinations; treat other backends as unspecified.

stories.title: Kimi K3.1 Support Lands in vLLM as a Split
whatHappened: vllm-project/vllm: [Model] Kimi K3.1: model files and NVIDIA specialized decode (Kimi K3.1 split 1/5) (#66030). vllm-project/vllm commit "[Model] Kimi K3.1: model files and NVIDIA specialized decode (Kimi K3.1 split 1/5) (#66030)" adds the model files and an NVIDIA-specific decode path.
A companion commit, "[Rust Frontend] Kimi K3.1 chat renderer (Kimi K3.1 split 2/5) (#66028)", adds the chat renderer to the Rust frontend.
mechanism: The split is structural: model definition, vendor-specialized decode kernels, and the frontend chat template are separate review units. The NVIDIA decode path implies the model's attention or MoE structure benefits from a hand-tuned kernel rather than the generic path, and the Rust frontend renderer means the newer serving frontend is now a required target for new model onboarding, not an afterthought.
whyItMatters: Two signals for serving operators: new model families will arrive with vendor-specific decode paths (so hardware choice affects day-one throughput), and the Rust frontend is accumulating real model coverage. Teams still on the Python frontend should expect divergence in chat-template behavior.
applicability: Inference platform teams planning Kimi K3.1 deployments on NVIDIA hardware. The commits are merge artifacts, not benchmarks — no throughput numbers are claimed here.

stories.title: vLLM Sleep Mode Level 2 Narrows to Discarding Parameters Only
whatHappened: vllm-project/vllm: [Sleep Mode] Level 2 discards only parameters (#66010). vllm-project/vllm commit "[Sleep Mode] Level 2 discards only parameters (#66010)" changes what the level-2 sleep state releases.
mechanism: Sleep mode is a memory-reclamation contract for serving processes that must yield GPU memory between jobs. Level 2 previously released more than weights; the change restricts it to parameters, which means KV cache and other allocations are handled differently — a narrower, more predictable release surface that avoids invalidating state the engine expects to keep.
whyItMatters: Sleep mode is how shared-GPU deployments time-slice a model server against other workloads. Changing what a level releases is a behavioral contract change: operators relying on level 2 to free KV cache memory will see different resident footprints.
applicability: Operators using vLLM sleep mode for GPU sharing or RL rollout/training co-location. The commit title states the scope; verify actual memory behavior against your workload rather than assuming a fixed savings.

stories.title: ROCm MoE Path Fixed for Count-Free Expert Metadata
whatHappened: vllm-project/vllm: [Bugfix][ROCm][MoE] Fix tkw1 rejecting count-free expert metadata, rename AITER QuantMethod (#65517). vllm-project/vllm commit "[Bugfix][ROCm][MoE] Fix tkw1 rejecting count-free expert metadata, rename AITER QuantMethod (#65517)" fixes the tkw1 kernel rejecting expert metadata that omits counts, and renames the AITER QuantMethod.
mechanism: MoE kernels receive per-token expert routing metadata; some producers emit metadata without explicit counts, deriving them implicitly. A kernel that requires counts rejects otherwise valid input. The fix relaxes that assumption on the AMD path, where AITER supplies the quantized MoE primitives.
whyItMatters: AMD MoE serving has been the weaker path, and failures like this are silent until a specific router output shape appears. The rename of QuantMethod is a small API break for anyone patching AITER integration directly.
applicability: Teams serving MoE models on ROCm. This is a targeted bugfix, not evidence of parity with the NVIDIA MoE path.

stories.title: SGLang Migrates NVLink One-Sided All-to-All onto FlashInfer's MoE EP
whatHappened: sgl-project/sglang: [Chore] [NVIDIA] deps: Bump FlashInfer to 0.7.3 and migrate the NVLink one-sided all-to-all to flashinfer.moe_ep (#48468). sgl-project/sglang commit "[Chore] [NVIDIA] deps: Bump FlashInfer to 0.7.3 and migrate the NVLink one-sided all-to-all to flashinfer.moe_ep (#48468)" bumps the FlashInfer dependency and moves the NVLink one-sided all-to-all implementation into flashinfer.moe_ep.

Separately, sglang commit "[Perf] dspark: Prepare the DSpark draft attention metadata through the glue graph under every verify mode (#48831)" changes draft attention metadata preparation for speculative decoding.
mechanism: Expert-parallel MoE dispatch over NVLink uses one-sided all-to-all so ranks can push tokens without paired receives. Moving that into FlashInfer centralizes the kernel in a shared library rather than maintaining a fork, which trades local control for upstream maintenance and version coupling. The dspark change routes draft attention metadata through the glue graph in all verify modes, removing a mode-dependent code path.
whyItMatters: Dependency consolidation in the MoE dispatch path reduces the number of places a correctness bug can hide, but it also means SGLang's EP performance now tracks FlashInfer releases. The dspark change matters for speculative decoding stability across verify modes.
applicability: SGLang operators running expert-parallel MoE on NVLink-connected NVIDIA GPUs, and teams using speculative decoding with dspark. No performance numbers are claimed in either commit.

stories.title: On-Policy Distillation vs GRPO, Measured in Training FLOPs
whatHappened: Preprint "Unpacking the Compute Efficiency of Strong-to-Weak OPD against GRPO" compares vanilla reverse-KL on-policy distillation — training a student on its own rollouts under a frozen teacher's per-token supervision — against Group Relative Policy Optimization across task difficulty, student and teacher size, domain, and optimization choices, measuring held-out accuracy against training FLOPs.
The abstract notes the comparison uses an external post-trained teacher. This is an unverified preprint.
mechanism: OPD supplies a dense per-token signal from the teacher on the student's own distribution; GRPO supplies a sparse, group-relative advantage from sampled rewards. Dense supervision should reduce the number of rollouts needed to reach a target accuracy, but it also requires a teacher forward pass per token — the FLOP accounting is what decides the trade.
whyItMatters: Most distillation-versus-RL comparisons report accuracy at fixed step counts, which hides the cost asymmetry. Framing the result as accuracy per training FLOP is the axis that actually determines which method a training team can afford.
applicability: RL and post-training teams with access to a stronger teacher model. Treat the specific crossover points as unverified until the paper is reviewed; the methodological framing is the durable takeaway.

stories.title: LoRA's Singular Spectrum Behaves Differently Under RL Than Under SFT
whatHappened: Preprint "Spectral and Subspace Dynamics of LoRA in Supervised Fine-Tuning and Reinforcement Learning" tracks the singular spectrum and subspaces of LoRA updates on mathematical reasoning tasks.

The authors report that RL concentrates the spectrum at every learning rate, while SFT expands it at moderate learning rates, and that RL rotates subspaces in a distinct pattern. This is an unverified preprint.
mechanism: LoRA optimizes a low-rank increment; the singular values of that increment describe how much capacity is allocated across directions. Concentration under RL suggests the update collapses onto a few high-value directions, consistent with reward-driven selection among a small set of behaviors, whereas SFT spreads capacity to fit broad next-token distributions.
whyItMatters: If the two stages shape the low-rank increment differently, carrying SFT-tuned LoRA hyperparameters (rank, learning rate, initialization) straight into RL is a category error. It also suggests rank is a stage-specific decision, not a model-specific constant.
applicability: Teams doing LoRA SFT followed by LoRA RL on reasoning tasks. The finding is on mathematical reasoning with specific optimizer settings — do not assume it transfers to other domains without checking.

stories.title: MCP Restores Optional _meta After SEP-2322 Silently Dropped It
whatHappened: modelcontextprotocol/specification: fix(schema): restore optional _meta on input requests and responses (#3469). modelcontextprotocol/specification commit "fix(schema): restore optional _meta on input requests and responses (#3469)" explains that SEP-2322 stopped these types from being standalone JSON-RPC messages: request params no longer extend TaskAugmentedRequestParams and results no longer extend Result.
Because both base types carried _meta, it was dropped as a side effect from CreateMessageRequestParams, ElicitRequestFormParams, ElicitRequestURLParams, ElicitResult, and ListRootsResult.
mechanism: Schema inheritance is a coupling mechanism: removing a base type to change message framing also removes every field that base contributed. Here the framing change was intentional and the field loss was collateral. The fix re-adds _meta explicitly rather than restoring the inheritance.
whyItMatters: _meta is the extension point MCP clients and servers use to attach out-of-band data without a spec revision. Its silent removal would have broken implementations that depend on it with no schema-level signal — a reminder that protocol refactors need field-level diffing, not just type-level review.
applicability: MCP client and server implementers, particularly those using _meta on elicitation or root-listing messages. Check your pinned spec version against this fix.

stories.title: Runtime Failure Monitors for Vision-Language-Action Models
whatHappened: Preprint "Failure Prediction and Classification in Vision-Language-Action Models Via Calibrated Latent Probing" presents VLA-Tug, a lightweight probe over the latent layers of a VLA model, arguing that deploying VLAs under distribution shift requires a runtime monitor that is timely, calibrated, informative, and edge-efficient.

A companion preprint, "T3R: Training-Free Two-Stage Token Refinement Towards Efficient and Robust VLA Models," targets inference cost by pruning spatially irrelevant visual tokens and refining attention over the rest. Both are unverified preprints.
mechanism: VLA-Tug reads internal latent states rather than output actions, so it can flag a failure before the action is executed; calibration is what makes the flag threshold meaningful. T3R attacks the same brittleness from the input side — hundreds of visual tokens per decision, many spatially irrelevant, distract action prediction under shift.
whyItMatters: Both papers treat VLA brittleness as an inference-time engineering problem rather than a training-data problem. That is the right framing for deployment: you cannot retrain your way out of every distribution shift, but you can monitor and prune.
applicability: Robotics teams deploying VLAs where failures damage equipment or endanger people. Latent probing requires access to model internals, which rules out closed API deployments.

stories.title: Bloomberg：OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元融资首批到账，估值达 1.25 万亿美元
whatHappened: AIHOT → X：Rohan Paul (@rohanpaul_ai) published “Bloomberg：OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元融资首批到账，估值达 1.25 万亿美元” on 2026-11-07. 据 Bloomberg，OpenAI 完成 110 亿美元新融资，这是估值 1.25 万亿美元一轮的首笔资金。投资者当日已打款，剩余部分总额最高 200 亿美元，预计数周内到账。 转引 Bloomberg 报道，给出本轮到账金额、整体估值和剩余资金节奏，可用于跟踪 OpenAI 融资进展。
mechanism: The durable product is the runtime: task handles, identity, sandbox restore, traces, and a kill switch. The model only picks the next action.
whyItMatters: Protocol and harness work (MCP, A2A, plugins, open runtimes) is where long jobs fail. Tool-calling demos hide that cost.
applicability: Prioritize if jobs run unattended. Skip the full runtime if a human is in the loop every turn.
